subject: Biology
title: Fertilization in Plants
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fertilization in Plants usable.

hook.text: When a pollen grain lands on the pistil, it grows a tube down to the ovule to deliver sperm cells.

buildup.text: The pollen tube can take hours to grow, pushing through tissue to reach the egg cell.

discovery.text: In flowering plants, double fertilization occurs—one sperm fertilizes the egg, another creates the endosperm.

twist.text: The endosperm is the starchy food supply for the developing embryo—it's what makes rice and wheat nutritious.

climax.text: Double fertilization is unique to flowering plants and helped make them Earth's dominant plant group.

punchline.text: Two fertilizations in one visit. Maximum efficiency.

quiz.question: What does double fertilization produce besides the embryo?

details.summary: Plant fertilization occurs when pollen delivers sperm cells to the egg inside the ovule. In flowering plants, double fertilization produces both an embryo and endosperm nutritive tissue. This unique process ensures the seed contains both a developing plant and its food supply.
details.whyItMatters: Double fertilization is unique to flowering plants and partly explains their dominance. Understanding plant fertilization is essential for agriculture, plant breeding, and developing crops that can withstand climate change pressures.
takeaways: Pollen tubes grow through the style to deliver sperm to the ovule
Double fertilization produces a diploid embryo and triploid endosperm simultaneously
Endosperm is the nutritive tissue that feeds the developing embryo in the seed

faq.question: What is double fertilization?
faq.answer: One sperm fuses with the egg to form the embryo. A second sperm fuses with polar nuclei to form endosperm, the nutrient tissue. This ensures energy-rich endosperm develops only when an embryo is present, avoiding wasted resources on unfertilized ovules.

faq.question: How does pollen reach the egg cell?
faq.answer: After landing on the stigma, a pollen grain grows a tube down through the style to the ovule. The tube can grow several centimeters in some species, guided by chemical signals. It delivers two sperm cells directly to the embryo sac for double fertilization.
